title: Shin Megami Tensei V
subtitle: A student walks into a ruined Tokyo
summary: Shin Megami Tensei V is Atlus's role-playing game, first released for Switch in Japan on 11 November 2021.
body: Shin Megami Tensei V is Atlus's role-playing game, first released for Switch in Japan on 11 November 2021. A Tokyo student enters the devastated realm of Da'at and becomes the Nahobino, drawn into a conflict among angels and demons over the world's future. Broad, ruined spaces give exploration an important place between encounters. The journey joins the scale of those landscapes to decisions about alliances and belief, while the demons encountered along the way can become the player's most useful companions.

The turn-based combat rewards exploiting weaknesses through the Press Turn system. A well-chosen attack can extend the party's opportunities, while a poorly matched element can squander them. The same logic applies to the enemy, making preparation and defensive resistance part of the plan. Exploration supplies information and resources for the next encounter, but the composition of the party determines how that knowledge can be used. A difficult opponent asks the player to reconsider its available attacks and protections rather than simply repeat the same sequence at a higher level.

Demons can be recruited through conversation and combined through fusion, carrying the party through successive changes as new abilities become useful. Masayuki Doi's designs and the music of Ryota Kozuka and Toshiki Konishi give the devastated world its particular atmosphere. Development began in 2016, combining ideas from Nocturne and Shin Megami Tensei IV. The expanded Vengeance edition followed on multiple platforms in 2024. The original Switch release establishes the central journey through Da'at, where the creatures being fought also supply the means of changing how the next battle unfolds.
